correctness.rationale: For n≥2k≥4, transitivity reduces a three-move Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé strategy to possible adjacency profiles of a fresh third vertex over a chosen distinct pair. For two k-sets intersecting in t∈[0,k−1], a fresh common neighbor exists exactly when n−2k+t≥k, i.e. t≥3k−n. Other three fresh adjacency patterns occur for all n≥2k+1; at n=2k the graph is a disjoint matching. Exhausting t gives exactly four pair-profile spectra: matching n=2k, low 2k+1≤n≤3k−2, boundary n=3k−1 and stable n≥3k, with least representatives 6,35,10,15 vertices. An independent implementation built actual full Kneser adjacency and fresh-pair profiles for (4,2),(7,3),(5,2),(6,2),(8,3),(9,3),(10,4), including n=2k matching case; all agreed. Kneser–Lovász chromatic number n−2k+2 yields unbounded k+1 on triangle-free n=3k−1 members despite rank-three equivalence. Finite checks corroborate, while pair-extension constructions and EF argument establish all parameters.
residual_risks: Restricted to nontrivial n≥2k≥4, standard adjacency-only FO without counting.
A three-round classification does not determine full elementary or four-round equivalence.

value.rationale: A complete natural finite-model-theoretic classification of an infinite two-parameter graph family. The logical collapse of triangle-free unbounded-chromatic graphs to Petersen at depth three illustrates a sharp expressive limitation, and the sharp 35-vertex representative is a useful exact invariant beyond isolated computations.
residual_risks: No implication at rank four, with counting quantifiers, or for edgeless/complete singleton-set variants.

limitations: Excludes k=1 and n<2k; rank 3 only.
Potential older FO theory classification not fully ruled out by bounded search.
